html:
Chiang Ching-kuo was the son of Chiang Kai-shek and leader of Taiwan from the 1970s until his death in 1988, as premier and then president. He was born in 1910 in Zhejiang, China, and spent twelve years in the Soviet Union as a young man.

In the 1950s he ran the secret police of the White Terror. As premier from 1972 he led the Ten Major Construction Projects, highways, ports and plants that pushed Taiwan's growth, and brought native Taiwanese into the Kuomintang.

In his last years he let the opposition Democratic Progressive Party form in 1986 and lifted martial law in 1987. He picked a Taiwan-born deputy, Lee Teng-hui, who carried reform on to the first direct presidential election.
